title: Hünkar Beğendi
description: A luxurious Ottoman-era Turkish dish featuring slow-braised tender lamb served over a silky smoky eggplant purée enriched with butter, milk, and cheese.

ingredients.title: Lamb Stew
items: 750 g lamb shoulder, cut into 3 cm cubes

ingredients.title: Eggplant Purée
items: 100 g Kashar cheese or mild cheddar, finely grated

instruction.title: Prepare the Eggplant
steps: Pierce the eggplants several times with a knife and roast them over an open flame, grill, or under a very hot broiler until the skins are completely charred and the flesh is soft.
Turn the eggplants regularly so they cook evenly and develop a deep smoky flavor.
Place the cooked eggplants in a bowl, cover briefly, then peel away the charred skins.
Drain the flesh thoroughly in a fine sieve to remove excess liquid.

instruction.title: Cook the Lamb
steps: Heat the olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Season the lamb with salt and black pepper, then sear in batches until deeply browned.
Remove the lamb and set aside.
Add the chopped onion to the same pot and cook until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they begin to break down.
Return the browned lamb to the pot and add the stock and bay leaf.
Cover and simmer gently for about 1 1/2 hours, or until the lamb is exceptionally tender.
Stir occasionally and reduce the sauce until rich and glossy.

instruction.title: Make the Eggplant Purée
steps: Finely chop or mash the drained roasted eggplant flesh until smooth but slightly textured.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the flour and whisk continuously for about 1 minute without allowing it to brown.
Gradually add the warm milk while whisking until smooth and creamy.
Add the roasted eggplant and stir continuously until fully incorporated.
Add the grated Kashar cheese and continue stirring until melted and silky.
Season with salt, black pepper, and a small amount of nutmeg.
Cook gently for another 3 to 5 minutes until the purée is thick, glossy, and spoonable.

instruction.title: Restaurant-Style Assembly
steps: Warm the serving plates before plating.
Spoon a generous layer of the silky eggplant purée onto each plate.
Create a shallow well in the center of the purée.
Place the tender lamb and its rich tomato sauce over the center.
Drizzle with a small amount of melted butter.
Finish with freshly chopped parsley and freshly ground black pepper.
Serve immediately while the eggplant purée and lamb are hot.

servingSuggestions.title: Ottoman-Style Presentation
items: Serve the lamb directly over the eggplant purée for the classic presentation.
Use warmed wide plates to create a refined restaurant-style appearance.
Garnish lightly with parsley rather than overwhelming the dish.
Serve with warm Turkish pide or crusty bread to absorb the sauce.
A simple shepherd salad with tomato, cucumber, onion, and herbs makes a refreshing accompaniment.

chefTips: Char the eggplant thoroughly—the smoky flavor is the defining character of the dish.
Drain the roasted eggplant well before making the purée so it does not become watery.
Brown the lamb deeply before braising to develop a rich, restaurant-quality flavor.
Cook the lamb slowly until it is tender enough to cut with a spoon.
Use warm milk when making the eggplant purée for a smoother texture.
Add the cheese gradually and stir continuously to create a silky, glossy purée.
Do not overpower the eggplant with spices; its smoky flavor should remain the star.
Serve immediately after plating for the best contrast between the hot lamb and creamy eggplant.
